target_customer: Plaintiff-side personal injury and employment law firms, plus agencies and MSOs that run several firms
problem: Plaintiff firms pay heavily for search ad leads, but the path from click or call to signed retainer is fragmented, with slow intake and no link between spend and signed cases.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus managed ad acquisition for law firms

founders.name: Rohit Sirosh
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led architecture of Azure high-throughput storage and worked with OpenAI on training workloads. Education not stated on the sources opened.

founders.name: Michael Korovkin
founders.background_notes: YC page gives first name only; surname from a YesPress profile. A secondary source says the founders have built together since 6th grade.

competitors.name: Eve
competitors.what: AI intake specialist and voice agent for plaintiff firms

competitors.name: Clio
competitors.what: Legal practice platform with Grow AI for intake and client development

technical_complexity.rationale: Ad channel management, a CRM for intake and spend to signed case attribution is standard integration work, with AI agents layered on top using existing models.

defensibility.rationale: A CRM holding intake and attribution data creates some lock-in, but intake AI is crowded and copyable in weeks by funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Eve launched a plaintiff intake product in 2025 and Lawmatics shipped AI intake agents in 2026, so well resourced players moved into the same wedge.

market_need_then: Plaintiff firms buy expensive high intent search leads and lose cases to slow response and poor spend tracking, per the company's launch pitch. Independent demand data was not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses trymimos.com, not the exact .com, as of 2026.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, concise, declarative, stresses human oversight (company site)

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand itself; a new two person company with a try prefix domain.

pivots.from: Answer engine optimization for regulated companies in health, finance and legal
pivots.to: Growth OS for plaintiff-side law firms
pivots.why: Reported by secondary profiles only; the stated reason is not given in a primary source.

outcome_analysis: Mimos is an active two person YC S25 company with no reported exit, shutdown or layoffs. It appears to have moved from answer engine optimization for regulated firms to a plaintiff law firm growth and intake product, where well funded intake specialists and legal CRMs are already shipping AI features. No traction numbers or priced rounds are public, so the outcome is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists a $500K pre-seed dated 2025-09 with Y Combinator only, Neuronfeed lists a $500K seed dated 2025-01, and a YesPress profile names XFactor Ventures. These are aggregators and conflict, so no round is recorded. Headquarters conflicts between New York and San Francisco. Pivot detail comes from secondary profiles. Education of both founders not found. Round recorded in the completeness pass rests on VCBacked (pre-seed 500K, 2025-09, YC); XFactor Ventures appears only in a YesPress profile (seed, Sept 2025). Neuronfeed dates a seed 2025-01 and StartupHub shows 5M for a different London entity; both disregarded.
